newsitem.title: UK: American urges BA tie approval as Star born.
newsitem.headline: American urges BA tie approval as Star born.

text.p: American Airlines reiterated its call to the UK and U.S. governments on Wednesday to push forward with the necessary approvals for its alliance with British Airways Plc.

Its latest call was prompted by the announcement of a new airline partnership called Star Alliance, which currently includes Deutsche Lufthansa AG, United Airlines, SAS, Air Canada, Thai International Airways Ltd and Varig.
American Airlines said in a statement released here that the announcement of the Star Alliance was a "good news/bad news" story.

"The good news is that the unveiling of the Star Alliance, which is far larger than the proposed American/BA alliance, will presumably end United Airlines' hypocritical opposition to our planned alliance," said Robert Crandall, chairman and chief executive of American Airlines.
American Airlines and BA announced their alliance plans nearly a year ago but their deal is still enmeshed in a complex web of regulatory processes.
Crandall said the "bad news" was that the Star Alliance highlights the regulatory delay on both sides of the Atlantic in its own alliance plans.
"We seek no special favour, only the right to compete with existing alliances, and to offer our customers a wider choice," Crandall said.
